Cleaning, waste & hygiene.

Set the cleaning scope by area and residue.

We organise agreed cleaning for shared areas, amenities and service spaces, as well as clean-up after maintenance. We identify the surface, level of soiling, waste type and access before setting the scope. Routine visits, deep cleaning and work-related clear-up are described as different tasks.

01 / Shared waiting area with hard floor finishes

Name the areas and the actual tasks

Routine cleaning can target the agreed high-use surfaces. Post-work cleaning first needs a list of dust, protective films, packaging and trade debris, with collection and specialist exclusions identified. Divide work by finish where methods or drying conditions differ.

Set cleaning frequencies by source and usage for recurring water marks, grit and back-of-house waste. Record surfaces requiring repair separately.

  • Shared spaces and amenities

    We agree the included floors, surfaces and fixtures, along with the required presentation and access. A room name alone is not a complete cleaning specification.

  • Service and waste areas

    We identify accessible surfaces, waste streams, temporary storage and collection routes. The brief distinguishes cleaning the area from transporting or disposing of its contents.

  • After maintenance or building work

    We define the agreed work-area clean-up and removal of related waste. Wider premises cleaning, retained stock and unrelated materials are identified separately.

A visit that follows the work list

Where grit reappears on a busy entry floor, note its source and the busiest crossing times. That record helps distinguish regular removal from work on damaged finishes or changes to waste handling.

  1. 01

    Confirm and prepare

    We check access, keys, site rules and included areas, then position equipment and protect retained items as agreed.

  2. 02

    Clean and collect

    We complete the specified tasks and segregate or collect the agreed waste, recording any condition outside the original allowance.

  3. 03

    Review and return

    We check the included areas, address agreed omissions and confirm removal or follow-up items before handing the space back.

Work around the people using the premises

We discuss occupancy, toilets and shared facilities, deliveries, storage and the time available for each area. The plan identifies temporary restrictions, equipment movement and the agreed return-to-use conditions. A restaurant, office and shared apartment area need different arrangements even when the floor area is similar.

When a terrace or entrance stays wet, we identify which areas have surface build-up and which collect water at a low point or blocked inlet. The cleaning scope covers the agreed surface and runoff arrangements. Loose paving and pooling that returns after rain go on a separate repair or drainage list, with walking routes managed during the work.

  • Quotation factors

Common questions

Does every repair include complete premises cleaning?
The quote states the included work-area clean-up. Cleaning beyond that area, additional waste and separate deep-cleaning tasks are defined individually so the scope remains clear.
How is a deep clean different from regular cleaning?
Regular visits follow an agreed recurring task list. A deep clean is scoped against specific surfaces and conditions, including any different equipment, preparation or access required.
Is waste transport and disposal included?
Record waste categories, quantities and access, then specify collection, transport and disposal by category.
